visual.caption: Typically left-sided; the splenic flexure is the most commonly affected watershed area.

events.x: Severe pain, frequent loose bloody stools

visuals.title: Treatment by type
head: Type
Definitive treatment
rows: Laparotomy, resect dead bowel, relook next day; embolectomy if not yet necrotic
Percutaneous transluminal angioplasty plus risk factor control
Supportive care and antibiotics; surgery if severe

visuals.title: The gut's blood supply
visuals.text: Clots from the heart (AF) travel down the aorta into the mesenteric arteries supplying the bowel.

visuals.title: Why watershed areas suffer
nodes: Distal ends of SMA and IMA get least

glossary.arterial embolus: A clot or debris that travels in the blood and lodges in an artery.
glossary.arterial thrombosis: A clot forming in an artery, usually on an atherosclerotic plaque.
glossary.venous thrombosis: A clot in a vein, here the mesenteric veins, blocking blood outflow.
glossary.hypoperfusion: Too little blood flow reaching tissues.
glossary.shock: Circulatory failure where tissues do not get enough oxygen.
glossary.valvular lesions: Diseased heart valves, which can shed clots.
glossary.low cardiac output: The heart pumping too little blood per minute.
glossary.vasculopathic: Having diseased blood vessels, for example from smoking, diabetes or atherosclerosis.
glossary.atherosclerotic: Caused by fatty plaques narrowing arteries.
glossary.out of proportion: Pain much worse than the gentle examination findings would suggest.
glossary.hyperactive phase: The first phase of ischaemic colitis, with severe pain and frequent loose bloody stools.
glossary.paralytic phase: When the ischaemic bowel stops moving, giving constant pain and distension.
glossary.bowel wall oedema: Swelling of the bowel wall with fluid.
glossary.abdominal X-ray: A plain X-ray film of the abdomen, also called an AXR.
glossary.mesenteric infarction: Death of bowel tissue because its mesenteric blood supply has failed.
glossary.evacuation of bowels: Passing the bowel contents, here suddenly and forcefully.
glossary.new-onset AF: Atrial fibrillation that has just started, a classic source of emboli.
glossary.guarding: Involuntary tensing of the abdominal muscles when pressed.
glossary.mesenteric vessels: The arteries and veins running in the mesentery to supply the bowel.
glossary.mesenteric arcades: Loops of linked arteries in the mesentery that feed the bowel wall.
glossary.arterial phase CT: A CT taken just as contrast fills the arteries, to show blockages.
glossary.HCO3: Bicarbonate, the main blood buffer; low in metabolic acidosis.
glossary.pCO2: Partial pressure of carbon dioxide; falls as breathing speeds up to compensate for acidosis.
glossary.pH: A measure of blood acidity; normal 7.35 to 7.45.
glossary.anaerobic metabolism: Making energy without oxygen, which produces lactate.
glossary.broad-spectrum: Covering a wide range of bacteria.
glossary.resection: Surgical removal of part of an organ.
glossary.non-viable: Dead or too damaged to recover.
glossary.risk factor modification: Reducing risks such as smoking, cholesterol and blood pressure.
glossary.supportive care: Fluids, rest and monitoring while the body recovers.
glossary.metabolic demand: The amount of oxygen and fuel a tissue needs.
glossary.peritoneal signs: Guarding, rebound tenderness and rigidity from an inflamed peritoneum.
glossary.arterial territories: The areas of tissue each artery supplies.
glossary.perforation: A hole through the full thickness of the bowel wall.
glossary.sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction from the body's response to infection.
glossary.food fear: Avoiding eating because meals bring on pain.
